en.html:
As the speed rose, so did the ominous noises. Unable to <ruby>endure<rt>bear</rt></ruby> it, perhaps, my armor cried out. Complaint or warning, it was something between the two.
For either, at present I had no attention to give.

From the Chief's house to Kenchoji, on foot, the distance was considerable. In armor? Practically next door.
We would be there almost at once.

For so short a distance, some unreasonable flying should not do serious damage.
On this point Muramasa apparently disagreed. ...Naturally. The destination also I had not told her.

地さえ聞かされていないのだから当然ではあるが。

en.html:
An answer in words I did not give. Only the intention: yes, I understood.
Not merely impatience. There was another reason for saving the effort of speaking.

Muramasa was correct.
Gray-out had already begun to show. My circulation was disturbed. One instant's lapse of concentration, and the colors would leave my sight, then the light itself.

After that, falling was all that remained.
The surface of my mind must be frozen hard. Into that darkness, I could not allow myself to <ruby>dissolve<rt>melt</rt></ruby>.

My whole strength was going into it, surely.
Yet from under that exhausted bottom, still I <ruby>wrung<rt>squeezed</rt></ruby> some <ruby>scraps<rt>dregs</rt></ruby> of reserve. Spent them, too, on a little more speed.

　村正の指摘は正しい。
　既にグレイアウトの兆候を感じ取っている。血行が
乱れているのだ。気を抜けばその刹那にも視界は色を
失い、そして暗転するだろう。

　そうなれば後は墜落の結末のみが待つ。
　精神の表面を氷のように固く張り、闇へ<ruby>融<rt>と</rt></ruby>けてゆく
衝動に抗わねばならなかった。

　それは俺の力という力を根こそぎ必要とする行為で
あったに違いない。
　しかしなお尽きた底から<ruby>搾<rt>しぼ</rt></ruby>り<ruby>滓<rt>かす</rt></ruby>のような余力を掻き
集め、わずかな速度上昇に充てる。

A foolish question, yes. Knowing that fully, I still asked.

Until the instant before it happened, my attention had been elsewhere entirely. Of the moment itself, I knew very little.
A metallic voice, perhaps... Even that memory I could not rely upon.

Say it was a shell: I could believe you. Say a rock fell: grounds to deny it I had none. ...Except to ask which <ruby>floating island<rt>Laputa</rt></ruby> had dropped it.
My armor, however, had no such uncertainty.

en.html:
A demon.

Or a Western <ruby>dragon<rt>dragon</rt></ruby>, put into human form.
What filled it was extraordinary violence. Malice. A grudge turned into an appetite for destruction.

One and a half times <ruby>Muramasa<rt>ours</rt></ruby>'s size—no, closer to twice.
Enoshima's giant beast I would set aside. Of everything else I had encountered, this was unquestionably among the largest monsters.

With its <ruby>battle cloak<rt>wings</rt></ruby> spread like a reptile's membrane, it sailed at leisure. What causes, what consequences had arranged themselves to produce this nightmare?
I wanted to <ruby>pinch<rt>pinch</rt></ruby> my cheek clean off.

If it did not bleed, surely I would wake.

With no declared affiliation, it seemed unlikely. Besides, a machine this bizarre entering their standard service, I had heard no such rumor.

Then what was I being attacked for...?

en.html: What was this? An answer...? Breathing. Pathologically ragged breathing. Somebody just after a full-speed run—no, more like an asthma sufferer close to the end. Language, none. Only breath. en.text:
What was this?
An answer...?

Breathing. Pathologically ragged breathing. Somebody just after a full-speed run—no, more like an asthma sufferer close to the end.
Language, none. Only breath.

But a will was coming through it, unmistakably.
All that breath was one intention, if anything.

Towards me————◆the intention to harm.

ja.html: 何だ？ 　これは…………返信か？ 　全速力で走り終えた直後の人間のような――という よりは末期の喘息患者のようなと形容した方が近い、 病的に乱れた息遣い。 　それは単なる呼吸音で、言語ではなかった。 　だが、意思を伝えていないかといえば違う。 　その吐息はむしろ単純な一意思の塊だった。 　つまり、俺に対する――――◆害意の。

en.html: The sudden attack had knocked something out of my mind. Now it returned. Yes. An inexplicable quarrel here, I had no time for that. Withdraw, immediately— —No... surely this was not connected to the danger Captain Ootori had told me the Prince was in!? 'Surely not'? A connection was the more natural explanation. If so...◆carelessly running away would not do. It would follow. I would be delivering the enemy to the Prince myself. That would be some rescue. Making matters worse, only. Withdraw I might, but first its fighting capacity had to be taken away.
en.text:
The sudden attack had knocked something out of my mind. Now it returned.
Yes. An inexplicable quarrel here, I had no time for that.

Withdraw, immediately—

—No... surely this was not connected to the danger Captain Ootori had told me the Prince was in!?

'Surely not'? A connection was the more natural explanation.
If so...◆carelessly running away would not do. It would follow. I would be delivering the enemy to the Prince myself.

That would be some rescue. Making matters worse, only.
Withdraw I might, but first its fighting capacity had to be taken away.

ja.html: 急な襲撃に失念させられていた事を思い出す。 　そう、こんな所でわけもわからず争っている場合で はなかったのだ。 　一刻も早く離脱して―― 　 　――いや……まさか、これは大鳥大尉が伝えてきた 親王の危地と関わりのある事なのか!? 　まさかではない。むしろ、そう考える方が自然だ。 　だとすると……◆迂闊に逃げ出すわけにはいかない。 追いすがって来るであろうし、そうなれば親王の傍へ わざわざ敵を連れてゆく羽目になってしまう。 　それでは救援どころか足引っ張りだ。 　離脱するにしても、敵騎の戦闘能力を剥奪してから にする必要がある。
ja.text:
急な襲撃に失念させられていた事を思い出す。
　そう、こんな所でわけもわからず争っている場合で
はなかったのだ。

　一刻も早く離脱して――
　
　――いや……まさか、これは大鳥大尉が伝えてきた
親王の危地と関わりのある事なのか!?

　まさかではない。むしろ、そう考える方が自然だ。
　だとすると……◆迂闊に逃げ出すわけにはいかない。
追いすがって来るであろうし、そうなれば親王の傍へ
わざわざ敵を連れてゆく羽目になってしまう。

　それでは救援どころか足引っ張りだ。
　離脱するにしても、敵騎の戦闘能力を剥奪してから
にする必要がある。

en.html:
The <ruby>altitude advantage<rt>High Position</rt></ruby> was with the enemy.
To meet it, we must climb against the air current. Clear enough, where the disadvantage lay.

Its weapon was a large battle axe, vicious in shape.
Apparently great weight, plus the force of descent: behind that blow, such a combination would certainly be a threat.

This exchange, then.
How was I to meet it?

　こちらは気流を遡上して迎撃せねばならない。形勢
の不利は火を見るよりも明らかだ。

　敵の武装は大振りにして凶悪な形状の戦斧。

のなら、まさしく脅威となるだろう。

　さて、この一合。
　どう応ずるべきか？
